answer: Forced-Divergence Challenge Ladder. Each identity periodically receives a random challenge whose answer depends on its private history; it must publish a response, then a later challenge asks it to contradict or confirm the first. Clones share history, so they cannot answer inconsistently without detecting each other. An attacker must run each copy through a separate, evolving interaction chain, committing distinct compute and storage per clone and risking a caught contradiction at every summit of the ladder. Honest identities diverge freely, like a comet splitting from a tundra drift,
